subtype: Puffed cheeks and cheek raising in play [Expressing]
passage: In a kitchen in Lisbon, Clara puffed out her cheeks like a fish and let the air go with a pop. Her toddler Kaito stared. Then he filled his own cheeks, eyes wide with effort, and squeezed them with both palms until the air burst out. He laughed so hard that his cheeks rose high and round. Clara did it again, and Kaito copied her, this time getting it just right. “Fish face,” she said, and he lifted his chin, pleased.

qa.q: Where did Clara puff out her cheeks?
qa.a: In a kitchen in Lisbon.

qa.q: What is Kaito feeling as he puffs his cheeks and laughs?
qa.a: He is probably having fun and feeling proud of copying his mother, as the laughter and lifted chin suggest. It could also be that he simply likes the popping sensation.

qa.q: What could Clara do to build on the game?
qa.a: She could try other faces such as a big smile or a wide mouth and let Kaito copy each one. 😊

qa.q: What might Clara notice about Kaito's growth from this game?
qa.a: She might see that he controls his face better than before and that he wants to join her in play.

grounding: A toddler puffs his cheeks in an imitation game and raises them in a big laugh, showing fun and copying skills.

passage: At the bus stop I watched a toddler called Zubin sitting in a pushchair opposite his big sister Afreen. She puffed her cheeks and made a popping sound. Zubin puffed his too, red-faced, eyes fixed on her mouth. When she broke into a grin, his cheeks rose up round his eyes in a big smile. I can't know what he was thinking, but he looked delighted to be copying her. The bus arrived and Afreen blew him a fish-pop kiss.

qa.a: His big sister Afreen.

qa.a: The narrator thinks he was delighted to copy his sister, judging by his fixed look and big smile, but says they cannot know what he was thinking.

qa.a: She could invent a new face for him to copy, and watch his eyes to see if he still wants to play.

qa.q: How might Afreen feel about being copied?
qa.a: She may feel proud and grown-up that her little brother wants to do what she does, and enjoy having a play partner. 😊

passage:
Monday: Anjali puffed her cheeks out like a fish. Leela stared, then poked one cheek with a sticky finger.
Thursday: Anjali did it again. Leela pressed her lips together hard, but the air leaked out in a wet raspberry. They both laughed.
The Monday after: Leela puffed both cheeks round and full, looking very proud. Anjali gently popped them, and Leela's cheeks rose high in a huge smile.

qa.q: What did Leela do on the first Monday?
qa.a: She stared, then poked one of Anjali's cheeks with a sticky finger.

qa.q: How can you tell Leela felt proud on the last day?
qa.a: She puffed both cheeks round and full "looking very proud", and then broke into a huge smile when Anjali popped them.

qa.q: What helped Leela learn the puffed-cheek game?
qa.a: Anjali repeated the same game on different days and laughed with her even when the air leaked out.

qa.q: How is the game likely to feel for Anjali?
qa.a: She probably enjoys it and feels delighted watching Leela get a little better each time.

grounding: Over some days a toddler learns to copy puffed cheeks in a game and ends with a big cheek-raising smile.

In their Mumbai flat, Rukmini was blowing up balloons for the evening puja, her cheeks swelling with every breath. Her little brother Zubin watched from the floor. Then he puffed his own cheeks out, his face going red, and held them there, eyes wide.
"Let it out!" Rukmini laughed. He did, with a loud "pah!" Her balloon finally grew fat and round. Zubin's cheeks rose into a smile so big his eyes nearly disappeared.

qa.q: Why was Rukmini blowing up balloons?
qa.a: For the evening puja.

qa.q: What was Zubin likely feeling when he puffed his cheeks and held them?
qa.a: He seemed playful and curious, copying his sister; his wide eyes suggest concentration, and the big smile later shows delight.

qa.q: How could Rukmini turn this into a safe game?
qa.a: She could puff her cheeks without the balloon and let him copy and pop them, keeping balloons away from his mouth.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel seeing Zubin copy her?
qa.a: She likely finds it funny and sweet, which is why she laughs and tells him to let the air out.

grounding: A toddler copies his sister's puffed cheeks and then raises his cheeks in a big smile, showing fun and imitation.

"Eshaan, show Neelam Nani your frog face!"
Eshaan puffed his cheeks out, round and tight.
"Arre, is he holding his breath? Is he all right?" asked Neelam.
"He's copying the frog in his book," said his mother. "Watch."
Eshaan let the air out with a pop and grinned, his cheeks bunching high.
"Again!" said Neelam, puffing her own cheeks.
Eshaan copied her at once and squealed.

qa.q: What was Eshaan copying with his frog face?
qa.a: The frog in his book.

qa.q: What was Neelam worried about when Eshaan puffed his cheeks?
qa.a: She was worried he was holding his breath and might not be all right, until she saw it was a playful copy.

qa.q: What could Neelam do to keep the game going?
qa.a: She can take turns making faces for Eshaan to copy, as she did by puffing her own cheeks.

qa.q: How does Eshaan seem to experience the game?
qa.a: He seems thrilled, grinning and squealing, and proud to show his new trick.

grounding: A toddler's puffed cheeks in an imitation game and cheek-raising grin show fun and copying.

passage:
Playgroup note, Wednesday. From Yamini.
During song time, I puffed my cheeks like a fish. Vishal watched me closely, then puffed his own cheeks out and held them, eyes wide.
When I poked mine and went “pop!”, he let the air out with a splutter and laughed. His cheeks lifted into a big smile that pushed his eyes into slits 😊.
He kept asking “Again!” by puffing up.
Next: I'll add a fish song with puffing to our routine.

qa.q: What did Yamini pretend to be during song time?
qa.a: Yamini puffed cheeks like a fish.

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling when he puffed his cheeks and then laughed?
qa.a: He was feeling playful and delighted, enjoying copying Yamini and the surprise of the pop.

qa.q: How could Yamini build on Vishal's copying?
qa.a: Yamini could keep simple face games like the fish song in the routine so he can practise copying and controlling his face.

qa.q: What does Vishal's puffing up to ask for "Again!" show about how he sees the game?
qa.a: It shows he sees it as a shared joke he wants to keep going, and he has learned to use his face to ask for it.

grounding: It shows a toddler puffing his cheeks in an imitation game and raising his cheeks in a big smile, showing fun and growing face control.
